title: New Journal Publishing Solutions Alliance Expands Options for Nonprofits
content:
Scholarly organizations seeking to develop or enhance independent journal publishing programs now have access to coordinated software and services through Allied Journal Publishing Solutions, an alliance between the Scholarly Publishing Collective, Scholastica, and Westchester Publishing Services. The alliance specifically supports nonprofit publishers, including scholarly societies and university presses.

Allied Journal Publishing Solutions gives publishers a flexible, integrated way to manage the full journal publishing workflow, with editorial management, production, hosting, sales, and fulfillment solutions from three trusted partners.

Available offerings include:

  • Powerful and intuitive peer review software from Scholastica
  • Editorial project management, copyediting, and production support from Westchester
  • XML, HTML, and print-ready PDF production through Westchester or Scholastica
  • Journal website hosting options (portfolio or individual) through SPC or Scholastica
  • Subscription management, sales, and customer service support through SPC

title: The MIT Press Thanks Library Partners for a Successful 2026 with Direct to Open (D2O) and Looks Ahead to the Next Funding Cycle
content:
Following the completion of our 2026 program cycle for Direct to Open (D2O), the MIT Press is pleased to announce the opening of our 2027 funding cycle, inviting libraries worldwide to support the innovative diamond open access model.

In 2026, library participation enabled a new collection of rigorously researched MIT Press scholarly books to be made openly available worldwide. This achievement reflects the ongoing commitment from more than 260 library partners to support collaborative models that expand access to high-quality monographs for those communities that need it most.

“We’re deeply grateful to all of our library partners who have invested in Direct to Open,” said Amy Brand, director and publisher of the MIT Press. “Reaching our full funding threshold for fiscal year 2026 demonstrates what’s possible when libraries and publishers work together to support equitable access to scholarship. We’re excited to build on that success as we move into our next fiscal year and adapt to the realities of modern scholarly publishing.”

title: Aries Systems and Imagetwin Partner to Enable Image Integrity Screening in the Editorial Workflow
content:
Aries Systems Corporation, a leading provider of workflow management technologies for the scholarly publishing community, and Imagetwin, an AI-powered image integrity software for research, are pleased to announce their partnership to strengthen trust in publishing through streamlined research image screening.

Research integrity is an increasingly complex and critical challenge within scholarly publishing. Ensuring research figures are credible within each article is typically a highly manual and time-consuming bottleneck for journals, and visual review by the human eye often fails to catch problematic cases. Without advanced support and additional resources, inconsistent image integrity investigations can result in frustrating delays and expensive post-publication corrections. To automate this process and minimize downstream risk, Aries Systems and Imagetwin have partnered to integrate their AI-powered image analysis software with Editorial Manager® (EM), the leading manuscript submission and peer review tracking system.

title: Read & Publish Open Access Agreement with the South African National Library and Information Consortium (Sanlic) Renewed for a Further Three Years
content:
The Company of Biologists is pleased to announce the renewal of our Read & Publish Open Access agreement with the South African National Library and Information Consortium (SANLiC). The renewal comes from a successful first agreement in South Africa with our representative in South Africa, Worldwide Information Services agency (WWIS), being influential in helping us establish our connection.

The agreement will run from 1 January 2027 until 31 December 2029, and corresponding authors at participating institutions can publish an uncapped number of research articles immediately Open Access (OA) in our hybrid journals (Development, Journal of Cell Science and Journal of Experimental Biology) and our fully Open Access journals (Disease Models & Mechanisms and Biology Open) without paying an article processing charge (APC). Researchers at participating institutions also benefit from unlimited access to our hybrid journals, including their full archives dating back to 1853.

title: Latest “Pulse Check” Poll focuses on Research Integrity in Scholarly Communications
content:
We are excited to announce the fifth Pulse Check poll to gather timely, actionable insights from across the scholarly communications community. 

Research integrity underpins the credibility, transparency, and long-term trust in scholarly communications, yet the challenges organizations face continue to evolve. This Pulse Check explores how organizations across the scholarly publishing ecosystem are responding to today’s research integrity challenges. The findings will provide a timely snapshot of current priorities, community confidence, and underlying causes.

Anyone in the SSP community is invited to take the poll, open through September 15.

Each Pulse Check poll consists of 5–6 focused questions, along with optional demographic information to enable richer segmentation and trend analysis.

A summary of key takeaways will be published in The Scholarly Kitchen, with an expanded report available on the SSP website.

We’d love to hear your ideas for future Pulse Check topics! Please share your thoughts at the end of the poll.

title: Publisher Collections on Jstor Expands Significantly for 2027, Growing from 22 to 36 Participating Publishers
content:
Beginning in January 2027, Publisher Collections on JSTOR will expand to 36 publishers, adding 14 new presses and renewing all 22 that joined when the program launched in January, 2026. Library participation is also growing, with a wide range of institutions in 10 countries participating, from community colleges and small private undergraduate institutions to large public universities. 

“As a mission-driven university press, our goal is to make scholarship available to as many researchers and students as possible,” said Brian Hughes, Sales and Marketing Director at New York University Press. “Publisher Collections on JSTOR is helping us reach new audiences and institutions—from R1 universities to community colleges—that we could not have reached on our own. That expanded access and engagement is an important measure of success for us.”

title: JSTOR Stewardship Introduces Alt Text Tools and Workflows for Image-Based Materials
content:
JSTOR Digital Stewardship Services has introduced new tools and workflows to support alt text for image-based materials across digital collections. With this release, Tier 2 and Tier 3 participants in JSTOR Stewardship can author, edit, export, and publish alt text on JSTOR. Tier 3 charter participants can also use JSTOR Seeklight to generate draft alt text for individual items or in bulk.

Alt text gives people who cannot perceive images access to information conveyed visually, and is a key part of meeting the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) for non-text content. For libraries, archives, and cultural heritage institutions managing large image collections, creating meaningful descriptions item by item can be difficult to scale. These new tools and workflows build on JSTOR’s commitment to accessibility and Stewardship’s accessible-by-design foundation by bringing support for WCAG-aligned alt text into the platform that institutions already use to manage and share their collections.

title: GeoScienceWorld Launches GeoSapienAI, an AI Research Assistant Built by the Geoscience Community for the Geoscience Community
content:
GeoScienceWorld (GSW) today announced the launch of GeoSapienAI, an AI research assistant developed in collaboration with leading geoscience societies to help researchers search, understand, and explore peer-reviewed geoscience literature.

Developed specifically for the geoscience community, GeoSapienAI searches and synthesizes information exclusively from GSW’s collection of peer-reviewed journals, books, and other scholarly publications contributed by its society partners. Every response includes citations and links to the original sources, allowing researchers to verify information, explore the underlying literature, and confidently build on existing research.

title: Data Conversion Laboratory and Bowker Publishing Services Collaborate to Meet Global Accessibility Standards for eBooks
content:
Combined Expertise Streamlines EPUB Accessibility Remediation

Data Conversion Laboratory (DCL), a leader in structured data and content transformations, and Bowker, a global leader in publishing services and the official ISBN Agency for the United States, have partnered to help publishers meet global accessibility standards for ebooks, combining DCL’s content transformation expertise with Bowker’s identifier and ebook services.

Bowker’s eBook Creator Suite gives publishers and independent authors flexible ebook conversion solutions for projects of every size, preparing content for global retail distribution. Powered by DCL’s conversion expertise, the enhanced suite now delivers accessibility by default across every service tier—from entry-level packages to the premier offering. By making accessibility a standard feature rather than an optional upgrade, Bowker and DCL help customers meet evolving industry requirements while expanding their global reach.
